The HTTPS certificate is set on the Torr: The HTTPS certificate is set on the TorrServer web page. The package runs with the limited rights that DSM gives it, so it does not read or copy DSM certificates itself.
Turn on HTTPS above, then save and resta: Turn on HTTPS above, then save and restart. Open the TorrServer web page, go to Settings, Additional, HTTPS and upload the certificate and the key.
A certificate uploaded this way is not r: A certificate uploaded this way is not renewed by itself. Upload it again after each renewal, or use one of the two options below.
Create a reverse proxy rule in DSM for t: Create a reverse proxy rule in DSM for the TorrServer port and assign your certificate to it in the DSM certificate settings. DSM renews the certificate by itself, and HTTPS can stay off in TorrServer.
Create a Task Scheduler task of the type: Create a Task Scheduler task of the type User-defined script. Run it as root, repeat it daily and use this script. It copies the DSM certificate to a folder of your choice and gives the TorrServer user access to it:
Then set the certificate and the key on: Then set the certificate and the key on the TorrServer web page to the two files in that folder. TorrServer re-reads them, so a renewed certificate is picked up without a restart.
If your certificate is for a domain and: If your certificate is for a domain and is not the default one, put its ID into the script. The IDs are the folder names in /usr/syno/etc/certificate/_archive.
